answer: Prompt architecture, concept art, vector assets, inpainting and colour: the still image made with diffusion models.

children.name: Prompt Architecture and Style Replication
children.blurb: Prompt architecture is the structured design of text prompts used to direct generative image models, including ordering, weighting, and the use of modifiers.

children.name: Concept Art and World-Building
children.blurb: Concept art and world-building use generative image models to produce exploratory visual designs for characters, environments, props, and cultural systems before production.

children.name: Vector Graphics and Interface Assets
children.blurb: Vector graphics and interface assets cover scalable two-dimensional artwork built from paths, points, curves, and fills rather than pixels.

children.name: Inpainting and Canvas Expansion
children.blurb: Inpainting and canvas expansion are two related techniques in generative illustration.

children.name: Algorithmic Colour Grading
children.blurb: Algorithmic colour grading refers to the use of software models to adjust hue, saturation, luminance, contrast, and colour balance across a still image or video sequence.

sections.body: This field covers still images made with diffusion models, from prompt architecture to concept art, vector assets, inpainting and colour. Artificial intelligence is now producing finished illustrations, concept sketches, interface icons and colour treatments in production pipelines. Prompt architecture and style replication work by turning a written description and reference images into a repeatable visual style. Concept art and world-building use these models to generate environments, characters and props before a project is fully designed. Vector graphics and interface assets are being generated as scalable shapes and UI elements, while inpainting and canvas expansion alter existing images by filling missing areas or extending a frame. Algorithmic colour grading applies learned colour transforms to stills, matching a target palette or mood.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The site tracks 1000 live image generation models, which shows the field is crowded but not settled. Prompt architecture can reproduce broad styles, yet exact replication of a living artist's hand remains unreliable and legally contested. Concept art generation is fast and often good enough for early exploration, but final art still needs human correction for anatomy, perspective and narrative intent. Vector asset generation is improving, though output often needs cleanup to meet interface standards for curves, alignment and file size. Inpainting and canvas expansion work well on simple backgrounds and textures, but complex scenes with overlapping objects or consistent lighting still show seams and artefacts. Algorithmic colour grading can match a reference palette, but it does not understand why a colour choice works in a scene, so it can flatten intentional contrast. The honest limits are that these tools accelerate drafts and variations, not replace a trained eye for finish.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from the first step of writing a prompt to the last step of colour finishing. Prompt Architecture and Style Replication is where a reader starts to understand how a text description becomes a repeatable visual style. Concept Art and World-Building then shows how those prompts are used to generate environments, characters and props for pre-production. Vector Graphics and Interface Assets shifts from painted images to clean, scalable shapes for screens and print. Inpainting and Canvas Expansion covers the repair and extension of existing images, which is often the bridge between a rough generation and a usable frame. Algorithmic Colour Grading ends the sequence by adjusting the final palette, so a reader can follow a single still image from prompt to graded output.
